content: Phenazopyridine is prescribed to alleviate pain, burning, irritation, and discomfort in the urinary tract. It also helps reduce the urgency and frequency of urination caused by urinary tract infections, surgeries, injuries, or diagnostic procedures. However, it is important to note that phenazopyridine is not an antibiotic and does not treat or cure infections. This medication may sometimes be prescribed for other uses, so consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Phenazopyridine is available in tablet form and is taken orally. It is typically taken three times a day after meals. The tablets should not be chewed or crushed; instead, they should be swallowed whole with a full glass of water. You may discontinue the medication once the pain and discomfort have completely resolved. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Take phenazopyridine exactly as directed, and do not take more or less of it or take it more frequently than prescribed by your doctor. Before taking phenazopyridine, inform your doctor and pharmacist if you are allergic to phenazopyridine or any other medications. Provide a list of all prescription and nonprescription medications you are currently taking, including vitamins. Notify your doctor if you have or have ever had kidney disease or glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency, an inherited blood disorder. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. If you become pregnant while taking phenazopyridine, contact your doctor immediately. If you forget to take a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular dosing schedule. Do not take a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Phenazopyridine may cause side effects. A harmless but common side effect is the discoloration of urine, which may turn red-orange or brown. If you experience any of the following mild side effects and they persist or worsen, inform your doctor: headache, dizziness, or upset stomach. Severe side effects require immediate medical attention. Contact your doctor if you experience yellowing of the skin or eyes, fever, confusion, skin discoloration (blue or bluish-purple), shortness of breath, skin rash, a sudden decrease in urine output, or swelling of the face, fingers, feet, or legs. If you experience a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA’s MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program online or by phone. Store phenazopyridine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture (do not store it in the bathroom). Dispose of any expired or unused medication properly. Consult your pharmacist for guidance on proper disposal. In case of an overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual has collapsed or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all appointments with your doctor and laboratory. Your doctor may order specific lab tests to monitor your response to phenazopyridine. Be aware that phenazopyridine can interfere with certain laboratory tests, including urine tests for glucose (sugar) and ketones. If you have diabetes, use Clinitest instead of Tes-Tape or Clinistix to test your urine for sugar. Tests for ketones, such as Acetest and Ketostix, may yield false results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctor that you are taking this medication before undergoing any tests. Phenazopyridine can stain clothing and contact lenses. Avoid wearing contact lenses while taking this medication. Do not share your medication with others. Your prescription is likely not refillable. If your symptoms persist after completing the course of phenazopyridine, contact your doctor.
